Vocation

/voh-KAY-shuhn/ - rhymes with location · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Vocation means a calling; work one feels especially drawn to do.

Restoring lighthouses paid little, but for Bea it was a vocation; she felt more herself on a scaffold above the sea than anywhere on land.

Worked Example

At the wildlife clinic where she had volunteered since she was twelve, Pia noticed that the burnout others described never touched her: splinting a hawk's wing at midnight left her lighter, not tired. Choosing veterinary school felt less like a decision, she said, than an admission - the work had chosen her first.

Vocation comes from the Latin for 'calling,' and that is exactly its claim: not merely work you do, but work you feel summoned to. A job pays; a career advances; a vocation pulls.

How Strong Is It? — job → career → vocation

job vs. vocation

job vs. vocation: A job is work that pays the rent; vocation claims far more - work you would feel incomplete without.

career vs. vocation

career vs. vocation: A career adds ambition and advancement to a job; vocation goes deeper still, naming work you feel called to whether or not it ever advances.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — voc-

Root — voc-: to call; voice

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: act or state of

Put it together

Put it together: Voc- (to call) + -ation (act or state of) = a calling. Latin vocare, 'to call,' is the same root that gives your voice its name. Medieval writers used vocation for a divine summons to religious life; English broadened it to any work that summons you. Its sibling vocational, also in this unit, drifted toward job training - see that card for the split.

Use the root in a new word: invoke

Use the root in a new word: invoke: The mayor invoked the town charter - called upon it by name - to cancel the crooked contract.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / warm

Vocation dignifies work as a calling, so save it for work someone feels pulled toward, not merely paid for; career is the neutral ladder-mate for paid advancement. And keep vocation apart from its look-alike relative vocational, this unit's other voc- word, which now means training for a trade - a plumber may have both a vocation and a vocational certificate, and the words are not interchangeable.
